summary: William Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1999–2006). He completed his MA under Richard E. Strassberg and his doctorate under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Dwight Whitney (1827–1894) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Williams College, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, von Roth, Lepsius, and Bopp, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Yale from 1853 to 1894.

William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He taught philosophy at Colby College (~2004–2008), was a professor at Marlboro College (~2008–2020), and served as a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Erskine (1773–1852) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1787 to 1792.
William Frederic Sinclair (1847–1900) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He was educated at the Royal School, Armagh, and joined the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a Sinologist who studied at Indiana University (~1966–1972) under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, and at the University of Bonn. In ~1979, he became Halls-Bascom Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
William Hunter (1755–1812) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1773–1777). He later served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society from circa 1802 to 1811.
William J. Johnson is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. His career includes academic posts at Cardiff University and the University of Wales.

William James (1842–1910) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Plymouth College and Harvard University—including Harvard Medical School and the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences—he held an academic post at Harvard from circa 1872 to 1907.

William Jones (1746–1794) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow School and University College, Oxford. In 1783, he was appointed Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William, and he founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech and the University of Washington (PhD ~1986 under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg) and held posts at JFK University and CIIS.

William L. Smith is an Indology scholar. He held a post at Stockholm University from circa 1976 to 2007, alongside positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Hampton University, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Kansas and Yale University (PhD under Stanley Weinstein), he became Professor of Asian Languages and Cultures at UCLA in ~1992.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from Connecticut College and a PhD from the University of Virginia (~1996–2006) under the supervision of David Germano.

William Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia (-1998) under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held posts at UVA, Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and Dharma Drum Buddhist College.

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) was a Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Chicago. He held posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania as E. Dale Saunders Professor in Japanese Studies.

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney (~1873–1875) and held posts at Denison University (~1876–1879) and the University of Chicago (~1891–1906).

William Robertson (1721–1793) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1733 to 1741 and later held a post there from circa 1762 to 1793.
William Roxburgh (1751–1815) studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1770–1772) and the University of Aberdeen (~1790). In 1793, he directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Columbia University (~1951–1955) and the University of Michigan (~1955–1960). He held posts at UC Berkeley (~1966–1995) and the Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2013).
